title: Even the winds obey (Matthew 8:23–34)
hookLine: a storm stilled, and a town that asks him to leave
tomorrow: why would a teacher answer his critics with homework?

lines: A TOWN ASKS HIM TO LEAVE.
cards: Neighborhood apps light up whenever something big changes on the block, and not every comment is glad. Here's the odd one in Matthew 8.
A town gets the kind of thing people pray for: two men nobody could pass on the road are set free. The whole city comes out. Not to thank him.
To ask him to leave. And the chapter's other scene is a boat filling with water while Jesus sleeps, and his friends shaking him: "Lord, save us: we perish."

teach.b: Start in the boat. Notice the order: Jesus speaks to his friends before the wind. "Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith?"
Then the great calm. Little faith is still faith: they were afraid, and they still woke him.

teach.h: WHAT MANNER OF MAN IS THIS?
teach.b: And they say what's on their minds: "What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!" They aren't asking his name. They're asking what kind of person a storm listens to.
Then the far shore, the country of the Gergesenes in the King James. Two men, exceeding fierce, coming out of the tombs.

teach.h: THE HERD RUNS INTO THE SEA.
teach.b: Jesus sends the devils into a herd of swine, and the herd runs down a steep place into the sea.

teach.h: THE CITY ASKS HIM TO GO.
teach.b: The herders run into the city and tell everything. Then the line that ends the chapter: "the whole city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts." So why?
Matthew never says. Maybe the lost herd. Maybe fear of a power that large, standing on their own road.
That's the puzzle's real answer: the same question, what manner of man, gets two reactions. In the boat, wonder. On the shore, fear enough to ask him to go.

how: Some Christians pray the disciples' cry, Lord, save us, in moments of fear, and some churches read the stilling of the storm aloud in their Sunday readings.

games.q: what does “even the winds obey” mean?
o: a saying about sailors' luck out on the sea
the disciples' wonder that a storm listens to him
a promise that faith always stops bad weather

games.q: the storm and the far shore — tap the pairs.
p: asleep as the waves covered it
ran down a steep place into the sea

s: Jesus was awake and anxious during the storm
he was asleep. his friends woke him: Lord, save us: we perish.
the town thanked Jesus and begged him to stay
they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.
Jesus speaks to the disciples before he calms the wind
why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? then the great calm.

games.q: a new manager fixes in a month what was broken for years. some coworkers are thrilled; a few ask to have her moved. what does Matthew 8 suggest is going on?
o: a change that big can cost people something, and that frightens.
the ones who complain simply hate anything good.
the fix must be fake, since real good never scares anyone.
games.why: Matthew never says why the city besought Jesus to depart. maybe the lost herd, maybe fear of a power that large. wonder and fear meet the same man.

practice: Close your eyes and let one part of your life come up where a change would cost you something: a habit, a grudge, a comfortable arrangement.
Notice, without judging, whether part of you would rather the change stayed on the far shore. Just notice it, and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Even the winds obey. The disciples' wonder in the boat, and the question under it: what manner of man is this?

orig.note: Greek: of what sort, what manner of. the disciples' question in Matthew 8:27.

carryVoice: Your line: what manner of man. A storm listens, and a town asks him to go. Go gently.
